title: The openrouter tool loop's bash tool refuses commands that reach past the node's worktree
name: loop-guard
description: packages/core/src/agent.ts runs every `bash` call as `sh -c <command>` in the worktree with no limit; ADR 0062 says the loop has no sandbox beyond the worktree. The file tools already refuse paths outside cwd (`withinCwd`), bash does not. Add a guard in front of `runBash`: at least `git push`, remote-changing git, `sudo`, and absolute or `..` paths that leave the worktree are refused, and the refusal goes back to the model as the tool result so the run continues rather than dying. Write down plainly what a string check on `sh -c` cannot stop (a script that builds the command at runtime) — in an ADR that amends 0062's Consequences, not implied as a sandbox. Tests in agent.test.ts cover a refused and an allowed command.

brief.approach: Keep the change inside the OpenRouter tool loop. Before `runBash` spawns `sh -c` in packages/core/src/agent.ts, conservatively inspect the requested command: refuse direct `git push` and other remote-changing git commands, `sudo`, and literal absolute or parent-relative path operands that resolve outside cwd; give the refusal as a normal bash tool result so the next model turn can correct its command. Permit ordinary local git/build commands and paths inside the worktree. Do not describe this textual check as a sandbox: quoting, shell expansion, runtime-built commands, symlinks and subprocesses can bypass textual inspection. Name those limits explicitly in a new ADR amending docs/adr/0062-sober-reaches-an-openai-compatible-endpoint-itself.md rather than changing ADR 0063. Extend packages/core/src/agent.test.ts at the tool-loop boundary to exercise denied commands (including an out-of-tree write attempt with no external effect), an allowed local command, and the subsequent successful turn after a refusal. Avoid new dependencies or unrelated host/dispatch changes. During work run only targeted tests; the approved acceptance commands run independently once the agent exits. Commit the work; do not push or merge.

acceptance.proves: The OpenRouter loop returns a refusal for prohibited direct bash commands without executing them, continues to the next turn, and still executes permitted in-worktree commands.

acceptance.run: pnpm exec biome check packages/core/src/agent.ts packages/core/src/agent.test.ts docs/adr && pnpm --filter @besober/core build
acceptance.proves: The changed loop compiles and its implementation, tests, and security-boundary ADR pass repository style checks.
